hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Western blots comparing membrane and total ABCA1 and ApoE in neonatal APOE3- and APOE4-targeted-replacement mouse primary astrocytes showed lower membrane ABCA1 with APOE4, with quantification from three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: However, membrane ABCA1 levels were significantly lower in ApoE4 primary astrocytes compared with ApoE3 ( Fig. 1 D , top, and F ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower cell-surface ABCA1 in primary mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cerebral cortical astrocytes from 1–3-day-old neonatal mice homozygous for human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted replacement, backcrossed onto C57BL/6J for 10 generations; no additional treatment specified; cell-surface biotinylation and NeutrAvidin isolation followed by Western blotting of membrane and total ABCA1 and ApoE.

rows.Finding description: Western blotting across three independent experiments showed higher ARF6 protein levels in APOE4 than APOE3 mouse primary astrocytes, providing indirect evidence about receptor recycling rather than measuring recycling itself.
rows.Finding quote: We found greater protein levels of ARF6 in ApoE4 primary astrocytes compared with ApoE3 primary astrocytes ( Fig. 1 H , I ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher ARF6 protein levels in mouse primary astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical astrocytes from 1–3-day-old neonatal human APOE3 or APOE4 homozygous targeted-replacement mice, backcrossed onto C57BL/6J for 10 generations; cultures enriched to 95% astrocytes after reaching confluence at 7–10 days and shaking for 16 hours; no additional treatment specified; ARF6 measured by Western blot with densitometric quantification.

rows.Finding description: ARF6 siRNA knockdown significantly increased 4-hour cholesterol efflux compared with scrambled siRNA in APOE4 mouse primary astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Knockdown of ARF6 by siRNA resulted in significant increase in cholesterol efflux in ApoE4 primary astrocytes after 4 and 24 h ( Fig. 3 C–E ).
rows.Finding summary: (ARF6 knockdown in APOE4 primary mouse astrocytes) -> (increased cholesterol efflux at 4 hours)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cerebral cortical astrocytes isolated from 1–3-day-old neonatal mice homozygous for human APOE4 targeted replacement, on a C57BL/6J background; cultures were approximately 95% astrocytes. Cells were transfected with 200 nM ARF6 siRNA or scrambled siRNA. Cholesterol efflux was measured over 4 hours using 3H-labeled cholesterol, calculated as medium radioactivity divided by total medium-plus-cell radioactivity.

rows.Finding description: In three independent experiments with ApoE4 primary mouse astrocytes, CS-6253 lowered total ARF6 (p < 0.001). Membrane ABCA1 was higher after treatment, and total ABCA1 showed no significant difference.
rows.Finding quote: CS-6253 increased the relative amount of ABCA1 on plasma membrane and significantly decreased total ARF6 protein expression in ApoE4-treated cells ( Fig. 5 A–C ). CS-6253 had no effect on total ABCA1 protein levels ( Fig. 5 A , C ).
rows.Finding summary: (untreated -> CS-6253-treated APOE4 primary astrocytes) -> (increased membrane ABCA1, decreased total ARF6, no change in total ABCA1)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical astrocytes from 1–3-day-old homozygous human APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups, on a C57BL/6J background after 10 backcross generations; cultures approximately 95% astrocytes; treated with or without 1 μM CS-6253 for 4 h; cell-surface biotinylation and NeutrAvidin isolation followed by Western blotting of membrane ABCA1 and ApoE and total ABCA1 and ARF6.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, treatment of APOE4 mouse primary astrocytes with 1 μM CS-6253 for 4 h increased membrane ABCA1 relative to control by Western blot densitometry; this rescue experiment did not compare APOE4 with APOE3.
rows.Finding quote: CS-6253 increased the relative amount of ABCA1 on plasma membrane and significantly decreased total ARF6 protein expression in ApoE4-treated cells ( Fig. 5 A–C ).
rows.Finding summary: (control -> CS-6253) -> (increased plasma membrane ABCA1 in APOE4 mouse primary astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical astrocytes isolated from 1–3-day-old human APOE4 homozygous targeted-replacement mouse pups, from mice backcrossed to C57BL/6J for 10 generations; treated with 1 μM CS-6253 for 4 h versus control. Surface proteins were biotinylated, isolated using NeutrAvidin agarose beads, and analyzed by Western blot densitometry.

rows.Finding description: Human HeLa cells expressing GFP-tagged ABCA1 were treated with 0.2 μM recombinant apoE4 or apoE3 for 30 minutes, and confocal imaging showed greater ABCA1–LAMP2 colocalization with apoE4.
rows.Finding quote: Greater colocalization of ABCA1 with the late endosome marker LAMP2 and lower colocalization with the recycling endosome marker Rab11 were observed in cells treated with rApoE4 compared with rApoE3 ( Fig. 2 ).
rows.Finding summary: (rApoE3 -> rApoE4) -> (greater ABCA1–LAMP2 colocalization in HeLa cells)
rows.Experimental system: Human HeLa cervical carcinoma cell line, provided by Dr. Alan Remaly, stably expressing ABCA1-GFP; treated with 0.2 μM recombinant apoE3 or apoE4 for 30 minutes; confocal fluorescence microscopy using anti-human LAMP2 staining to assess late-endosomal/lysosomal ABCA1 localization. These are non-brain cells; recycling kinetics and ARF6 involvement were not directly measured in this panel.

rows.Finding description: In human HeLa cells expressing GFP-tagged ABCA1 and treated with recombinant apoE4 for 30 minutes, adding CS-6253 increased ABCA1–Rab11 colocalization by 11%; this rescue comparison held apoE4 constant and measured recycling-endosomal localization rather than recycling rate.
rows.Finding quote: Compared with cells treated with rApoE4 only, ABCA1 colocalization with Rab11 significantly increased by 11% upon cotreating cells with rApoE4 plus CS-6253 and by 12% with CS-6253 alone ( Fig. 6 A , B ).
rows.Finding summary: (rApoE4 alone -> rApoE4 + CS-6253) -> (increased ABCA1–Rab11 colocalization in HeLa cells)
rows.Experimental system: Human HeLa cells, provided by Dr. Alan Remaly and stably transfected with ABCA1-GFP, treated with 0.2 μM recombinant apoE4 with or without 1 μM CS-6253 for 30 minutes; confocal immunofluorescence assessed ABCA1 colocalization with the recycling-endosome marker Rab11.

rows.Finding description: In APOE4 mouse primary astrocytes treated with ARF6 or scrambled siRNA, combining ARF6 reduction with CS-6253 produced a small but significant additional increase in cholesterol efflux, a surrogate readout of recycling, without an APOE3 comparison.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE4 primary astrocytes had a small but significant increase in cholesterol efflux after reducing ARF6 protein and the addition of CS-6253 ( Fig. 7 B ).
rows.Finding summary: With CS-6253 present in both groups, ARF6 siRNA increased cholesterol efflux relative to scrambled siRNA in ApoE4 mouse primary astrocytes.
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical astrocytes from 1–3-day-old human APOE4 homozygous targeted-replacement mouse pups; mouse lines backcrossed to C57BL/6J for 10 generations. Cells received ARF6 or scrambled siRNA (200 nM final concentration), followed by 3H-cholesterol labeling for 24 h, PBS washing, and CS-6253 treatment for 4 h. Cholesterol efflux was measured as medium radioactivity divided by total medium-plus-cell radioactivity.
